title: Snapshot Governance: Updated Voting Framework
headline: The Compound Governance Working Group proposes new eligibility rules for voting and proposing in the comp-vote.eth Snapshot space; onchain governance is unchanged.
summary: This post introduces an updated voting framework for the comp-vote.eth Snapshot space, run by the Compound Governance Working Group (CGWG). It applies only to Snapshot. Onchain voting and execution through the Compound Governor stay as they are, and no new space is created. To vote, an address must meet three criteria: be identifiable through a forum delegate profile, a known individual or organization, existing CGWG voter records, or an ENS or Tally name; hold at least 1 COMP of eligible delegated voting power at the proposal reference block; and have voted on at least five distinct Compound proposals in the prior 12 months, or pass a CGWG review. Delegates who moved to a new address can carry over voting history. The framework also applies security exclusions to addresses the post says are linked onchain to the dCOMP voting position. As background, the post cites the Foundation published record, which alleges malicious governance activity since 2024, and notes the Proposal Guardian recently cancelled Proposals 612, 613, 618 and 619. These allegations are the post authors position and are not verified here. Open questions include how identity and coordination evidence are judged.
